recent_posts.title: Why contra dancing is one of the most accessible and joyful activities you can try
recent_posts.summary: A personal essay advocating for contra dancing as one of the most accessible and joyful physical activities to pick up. The author shares their origin story from reluctant middle schooler to enthusiast, explains the mechanics (long-line group folk dance with a live band and a caller), and argues that contra's low barrier to entry, welcoming community, and intergenerational nature make it an ideal starting point for anyone interested in dance. The post also frames contra as an antidote to modern life's screen-heavy, atomized, irony-saturated culture, and closes with practical tips on finding a local dance, what to wear, and how to improve.

recent_posts.title: Impact, agency, and taste
recent_posts.summary: Discover what sets apart highly effective coworkers at Anthropic through their ability to find and execute high leverage work. Key components include working on impactful projects such as improving tools, identifying research directions, and system design. Enhancing impact involves developing agency and taste, where agency is about the proactiveness to execute, and taste is intuition for identifying and solving essential problems. Strategies for improvement include practicing, understanding goals, not relying too much on permission, making success inevitable, finding unique strengths, and continuously reflecting on decisions and processes.

recent_posts.title: Advice for time management as a manager
recent_posts.summary: Managing time as a manager requires juggling competing priorities, focusing on team output, and adopting a manager's schedule. Key strategies include having realistic expectations, prioritizing tasks ruthlessly, delegating effectively, and carving out focused time for deep work. It's also important to have a plan for when you feel overwhelmed.

recent_posts.title: How I’ve run major projects
recent_posts.summary: Effective project management involves focus, maintaining a detailed plan, running a fast OODA loop, overcommunication, breaking off subprojects, and enjoying the process. Clear goals and priorities help to manage large projects, especially in crisis mode. Detailed planning, fast information processing, and high levels of communication are essential. Delegating management tasks efficiently and keeping project goals simple can significantly improve execution.

recent_posts.title: Categories of leadership on technical teams
recent_posts.summary: Effective team leadership in tech involves multiple key responsibilities: overall direction, people management, project management, and technical leadership. Dividing these responsibilities among different team members can help leverage individual strengths and improve team productivity. Various models, such as the 'tech lead manager' or an 'engineering manager/tech lead' split, illustrate different ways to structure these roles depending on team size, complexity, and objectives.

recent_posts.title: Trust as a bottleneck to growing teams quickly
recent_posts.summary: Trust is crucial for effective teamwork, especially in fast-growing companies. Lack of trust can slow down decision-making and require thorough supervision, hampering efficiency. Building trust involves sharing mental models, frequent communication, trial tasks, feedback, and proactive status updates. Recognizing and addressing trust deficits can enhance overall team performance and collaboration.

recent_posts.title: Leaving Wave, joining Anthropic
recent_posts.summary: The author is leaving Wave after 8 years and joining Anthropic due to concerns about AI and the potential impact on society.

recent_posts.title: Why and how to write things on the Internet
recent_posts.summary: Discover the benefits of starting a blog and how it can lead to more friendships. Learn tips for writing things on the Internet and building a consistent writing habit.

recent_posts.title: Staring into the abyss as a core life skill
recent_posts.summary: Staring into the abyss is a core life skill that involves thinking about uncomfortable topics and making difficult decisions. It requires acknowledging past mistakes and facing uncomfortable truths. Many successful people exhibit this skill and it is important for personal growth and effective decision-making. To become better at abyss-staring, one can learn from experienced individuals, seek out uncomfortable questions, and time their introspection appropriately. Asking uncomfortable but productive questions may help uncover hidden desires and motivations.

recent_posts.title: Be less scared of overconfidence
recent_posts.summary: The author reflects on their past decisions and highlights the problem of relying too heavily on low-info heuristics. They discuss situations where they threw away valuable information in fear of overconfidence and wishful thinking. The author emphasizes the importance of being ambitious and searching for outliers instead of blindly following general heuristics.
